rows.current: 朝は味噌の汁を飲みます
rows.why: The eight mode-C tokens are a faithful parse of the stored jp: no boundary, reading, lemma or gloss defect exists against it, and position 2 (味噌) carries vocab_id 971, which is this record's declared target word (tag 971). Only the pending jp change makes the array stale, and it cannot be re-run blind: the vocab registry has 味噌 (971) and 汁 (3551) as separate entries and no entry for the compound 味噌汁, so a merged token comes back with vocab_id null and the sentence loses its only link to its target word. Whether mode C even returns 味噌汁 as one morpheme is analyzer output. Note also that position 4 (汁) already carries vocab_id null although entry 3551 exists, so this record's links predate part of the registry.

Wrong lemma link on position 0. The token 背 is read せ, but it points at entry 336, whose kana is せい; the entry whose kana is せ is 1338, which is also this record's declared target vocab (tag 1338). dissect.py resolves links through a form table keyed on the written form alone (_vocab_id in scripts/ingest/dissect.py), so the reading is never consulted and the first entry registered for 背 wins. 12 tokens read せ carry the 336 link corpus-wide. This applies to the array as it stands; if the 背中 re-author in the jp queue is accepted instead, position 0 is replaced and entry 1229 (背中) becomes the link.

rows.current: 背がいたいので病院に行く
rows.why: Two defects that a re-run will not settle. First, particle mis-analysis: ので is held as two tokens, position 3 の tagged 準体助詞 and position 4 で lemmatised to the copula だ in the continuative, and both carry null role and null gloss, so the learner-facing breakdown shows an unexplained で and the record's own explanation apologises for the split. The correct unit is the single conjunctive particle ので, which is a mode-C boundary outcome. Second, gloss mismatch on position 0: the gloss reads back and costas, but both 背 entries in the registry (336 and 1338) gloss as height and stature, so the gloss matches neither the linked lemma nor the target. Accepting the queue's 背中 re-author removes target vocab 1338 from the sentence altogether, which is a content decision, not a parse decision.

rows.current: お金をためて、然うして車を買った
rows.why: Boundary error that breaks the target-vocab link. The declared target is entry 1340 (然うして, kana そうして), and the dissection never links it: mode C cut the conjunction into three tokens, position 5 然う as an adverb with vocab_id null, position 6 し, and position 7 て, so the record's own target word has no anchor. Two homophone mis-links ride along: position 6 し links entry 334 (刷る, to print) where the verb is する, entry 1358 (為る); and position 2 ため, lemma ためる, links entry 1089 (為, for the sake of) where the verb entry is 3725 (溜める, ためる). Restoring one 然うして token is analyzer output, and the orthography change proposed in the jp queue does not by itself force the merge, since 然うして and そうして are registered as two forms of the same entry. This record also carries mode-A subunits (お, 金) at array indices 0 and 1, so array index and position do not agree here.

rows.current: あの店は安くはないが おいしい
rows.fix: あの店は安くはないが おいしい
rows.why: The complaint is stale. Position 7 is the stray U+0020 and its reading and romaji are already blank, so no phantom きごう or kigou is present anywhere: kana is あのみせわやすくわないがおいしい and romaji is anomisewayasukuwanaigaoishii, and the concatenated C-token readings reproduce kana exactly. scripts/fable5_fix_whitespace_tokens.py already repaired this class corpus-wide and deliberately leaves jp alone, because deleting the space breaks the invariant that concatenated C-token surfaces equal jp, and because in other records the space separates two sentences. The queue's proposal to write a single space into this token's reading and romaji would reinsert that space into kana and undo the repair. If the space is nevertheless dropped from jp, the token has to be deleted in the same operation and おいしい renumbered from position 8 to position 7.

The pending particle correction touches exactly one slot, because で and に are both one-character 格助詞: position 2 takes surface, lemma and reading に with romaji ni, the C-token count stays at 7, no other position shifts, and no vocab link moves (particles are never linked). Boundary-neutral orthography change confined to position 0. Its reading ここ, romaji koko, pronoun POS and vocab_id 246 already describe the kana form, and entry 246 is headword 此処 with kana ここ, so the link survives: dissect.py indexes vocab by kana as well as by headword and form. lemma is taken from dictionary_form, not normalized_form (scripts/ingest/dissect.py line 159), so the ateji does not creep back in through the lemma field. C-token count stays at 5.

POS mis-analysis caused by the kana spelling. Position 3 is the direct object of 描く, it carries vocab_id 85 (絵, picture, drawing), its role says direct object and its gloss spells the kanji out as drawing (絵) as a workaround, yet the analyzer tagged it 感動詞 フィラー, the filler interjection え. The vocab link already points at the right lexeme, so only the surface and the three POS fields disagree with it. This edit must be applied together with the jp value 厚い紙に絵を描いた from the jp queue, otherwise the concatenated C-token surfaces stop reproducing jp. Not a defect: the reading えがい on position 5 is a legitimate alternative to かい for 描いた, and kana and romaji are already consistent with it.

Two defects that pull in opposite directions. Gloss does not match the token: 手の裏 is dictionary-defined as the palm, the same referent as 手のひら, while the back of the hand is 手の甲; both locales of this gloss say the opposite, and so do both translations. Target vocab unlinked: the declared target is entry 1088 (裏, うら) and no token links it, because 手の裏 was taken as a single 普通名詞 with vocab_id null, which also hides the internal の from the breakdown. Correcting the gloss alone leaves a sentence whose translations contradict it; taking the queue's 紙の裏 splits the single token into three and restores a 裏 link, but that is a re-parse plus a content decision about what the sentence teaches.

rows.current: closing こ of はこ (箱, 'box') plus the genitive の

Mode C read このはこの as この + は + この, so position 2 spans the last mora of はこ plus the following の, and the corpus wrote the explanation of that error into the token's own gloss and role instead of correcting the cut. The correct analysis is この + はこ + の. Two pieces of corroborating damage sit on the affected span: position 1 had its reading hand-corrected to は while its romaji still holds wa from the particle override, so the concatenated token romaji reads konowa where the sentence romaji reads konoha; and position 2 links vocab_id 196 (九) as though it were the demonstrative. No re-run of mode C will produce the correct cut on this unspaced kana string, so this needs a manual token override of the kind already registered for readings, and the gloss and role text on position 2 have to go with it.

Stale token romaji on position 8. The token 中 had its reading hand-corrected to なか, but its romaji still holds chuu, the romanization of the analyzer's original ちゅう; the stored sentence romaji already reads naka, so only the token field is wrong. This is one instance of a class: 336 of the 5,565 sentences in the bank have C-token romaji that no longer concatenates to the stored sentence romaji, while the kana concatenation still matches in all 5,565. That is the fingerprint of the verified-reading-override pass rebuilding readings and the sentence-level fields without recomputing token romaji, which dissect.py derives from the token reading (_tok_romaji, with the は, へ and を particle overrides preserved).

summary: 23 sentences, 39 rows: 28 fix, 2 no-change, 9 needs-human. Two of the queue's own complaints do not survive contact with the file. The whitespace record (sent:gen-68448be6940b) has no きごう leak left: reading and romaji on that token are already blank and kana and romaji are clean, and the proposed edit would reinsert a space into kana and undo the audited corpus-wide repair. The reorder record (sent:gen-bc13250dc26f) has no dissection defect at all; its ten tokens only need permuting, with no analyzer involved. The dominant real defect in this queue is not boundaries, it is wrong lemma links: 12 rows repoint a vocab_id, and in six records (67098aef1bd0, 6f1566f1c7de, efb21932a32f, 986d061ae368, 960cef5443b3, 7dd5dc18aba8) the sentence has no link at all to the very word it was generated to teach. Links are made by a form-table lookup in scripts/ingest/dissect.py that keys on the written form alone and keeps whichever entry was registered first, so reading and POS never enter the decision. Every mis-link found here has a correct entry already in the registry, and the classes run corpus-wide, far past this queue: する and し to 334 (刷る) 716 tokens, この to 196 (九) 367, かれ to 41 (彼 あれ) 297, なか to 79 (内) 57, せ to 336 (背 せい) 12, よう to 1176 (様 さま) 7, 尤も to 1184 (最も) 3, 下る to 1178 (下がる) 2, ためる to 1089 (為) 1. Repointing する and かれ crosses an n5/n4 boundary, so level coverage counts move with them. Second systematic finding: token romaji is stale in 336 of 5,565 sentences, where the concatenated C-token romaji no longer equals the stored sentence romaji, while kana still concatenates correctly in all 5,565. That is the residue of the verified-reading-override pass, which corrected readings and the sentence-level fields but never recomputed token romaji; sent:tatoeba-223377 is the instance inside this queue. Third, an addressing hazard the applying pass must handle before anything else: in records carrying mode-A subunits the tokens array is not indexable by position, because the A rows sit ahead of every C row. Two records here are affected, and for sent:gen-cb6562f41e17 the queue's four tokens[0] edits land on the honorific prefix お instead of 私. Token paths have to be resolved by the position field with split_mode C. The needs-human rows split into three kinds: boundary merges only the analyzer or a registered manual override can deliver (味噌汁, そうして, ので, 学生はいない, １日 as ついたち, このはこの); content decisions that change what a sentence teaches (背 against 背中, 手の裏 against 紙の裏); and one Layer-A integrity question (sent:tatoeba-141147, where the recorded jp and its paired English disagree and the check belongs upstream against Tatoeba, not in the token array). On sent:gen-960cef5443b3 the earlier rejection was right: ついたち is a fused reading and must never be stored as つい on １ and たち on 日.
